messages.recipient_title: Executive Vice President Marine and Asset Operations
messages.subject: For Marianne Møgster | Sustainability, Stakeholder Governance & Offshore Energy Leadership | Executive Proposal
messages.body:
Dear Ms. Møgster,

I am writing from Guyana, where I serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My work spans ESG, government relations, regulatory coordination, stakeholder strategy and executive issue management inside a major multinational resource operation.

DOF's global offshore-energy platform, marine operations and sustainability agenda strongly align with the problems I manage today: connecting operating priorities with regulators and public institutions, converting sustainability commitments into accountable action and coordinating complex external issues across business functions.

I prepared a DOF-specific Strategic Value Creation Proposal rather than sending a conventional CV alone. It sets out where I would add value across sustainability governance, external affairs, stakeholder intelligence, responsible operations and international market engagement. My three-page Executive CV forms the final section.

I am open to relocation to Norway and employer-supported work authorization. My strongest fit would be a Director, Head, Country, Regional or senior leadership mandate across Sustainability, External Affairs, Government Relations, Strategic Partnerships, Stakeholder Management or responsible operations.

I would value a short confidential conversation. If another senior leader owns the most relevant mandate, I would be grateful if you would route the proposal internally.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility
AGM Inc. | Zijin Mining Group
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposal: Sustainability, Stakeholder Governance and Offshore Energy Leadership
strategic_brief.prepared_for_title: Executive Vice President Marine and Asset Operations
strategic_brief.executive_summary: DOF operates a global marine and subsea platform supporting offshore energy across multiple jurisdictions, with approximately 6,000 people and a substantial international fleet. That model depends on more than technical and operational performance. Regulatory confidence, sustainability governance, human-rights standards, stakeholder alignment and disciplined external engagement all influence the company's ability to execute reliably and grow. I bring director-level experience from a multinational resource operation where government relations, ESG, regulatory coordination and cross-functional stakeholder management are integrated into operating decisions. My contribution would be to strengthen the link between external expectations, sustainability commitments and accountable execution across complex country and asset interfaces.
strategic_brief.company_context: DOF is a Norwegian-headquartered provider of integrated marine and subsea services to the global offshore energy market. Its management team includes senior leadership spanning marine and asset operations, people and organisation, finance and other group functions, and Marianne Møgster previously held the EVP Sustainability mandate before moving into her current operating leadership role. DOF has also publicly positioned human rights, responsible supply chains and sustainability reporting as important parts of its governance model. The combination of global marine operations, energy-sector exposure and international stakeholder requirements creates a strong case for tightly linking ESG, institutional intelligence, responsible-business obligations and operating execution. Such integration helps leadership anticipate issues earlier, clarify ownership and maintain consistent standards across jurisdictions.

opportunities.title: Country and stakeholder intelligence
opportunities.rationale: Marine and subsea operations interact with regulators, port authorities, energy companies, public institutions and local stakeholders across multiple markets. Material issues often emerge locally before they become visible through central reporting systems.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would establish a concise country and stakeholder intelligence framework that ranks external developments by materiality, assigns response ownership and links institutional signals to operating and executive decisions.

opportunities.title: Sustainability commitment governance
opportunities.rationale: Global operators accumulate sustainability and responsible-business commitments across customers, regulators, financiers and internal governance processes. Risk rises when commitments are not translated into accountable owners, evidence requirements and closure records.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would strengthen commitment registers, ownership and review routines so external obligations are connected to operating functions, milestones, evidence and executive escalation.

opportunities.title: Responsible operations and human rights
opportunities.rationale: DOF's public work on responsible supply chains and human rights requires strong coordination across procurement, people, operations, legal and sustainability functions. Practical governance is essential when risks span jurisdictions and contractor networks.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support a cross-functional operating model that links responsible-business risks to clear controls, stakeholder engagement, evidence trails and timely management action.

opportunities.title: External affairs supporting international growth
opportunities.rationale: Offshore-energy growth increasingly depends on institutional relationships, permitting environments, local-content expectations and strategic partnerships alongside technical capability. These factors can shape market access and execution economics.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support selected growth markets with government engagement, regulatory coordination, stakeholder mapping and strategic partnership development grounded in direct resource-sector operating experience.

days_0_30: Map priority regulatory, stakeholder and sustainability interfaces across selected countries and operating functions.
Review material commitments and identify ownership, evidence or escalation gaps.
days_31_60: Introduce a pilot country-intelligence and commitments framework linked to operating priorities.
Align selected responsible-business and sustainability obligations with accountable internal owners.
days_61_90: Use live market and stakeholder issues to test the framework and improve executive visibility.
Deliver a dashboard covering material external developments, commitments, evidence status and management action.
days_91_180: Scale the strongest methods across additional countries or operating interfaces.
Measure results through issue closure, stakeholder outcomes, assurance readiness and reduced execution surprises.

potential_impact: Earlier visibility of material regulatory and stakeholder risks across international operations.
Stronger accountability behind sustainability and responsible-business commitments.
More consistent management of human-rights and contractor-related obligations across jurisdictions.
Closer integration of external affairs, sustainability and operating execution.
background_relevance: Director-level experience spanning ESG, government relations, regulatory coordination, corporate affairs, social responsibility and executive advisory in a multinational resource company.
Experience coordinating regulators, ministries, contractors and internal operating functions around external obligations and major business priorities.
Practical experience with renewable-energy deployment, carbon-data governance and evidence traceability in a regulated industrial setting.
Direct emerging-market experience where local-content expectations, public institutions, infrastructure and stakeholder legitimacy materially affect project execution.
